stories.title: Iran's supreme leader warns US, Israel of 'unrestricted geographical response' to new attacks
summary: The remarks came during a reported meeting between Khamenei and senior military commanders, including armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, army chief Amir Hatami and Revolutionary Guards commander Ahmad Vahidi.
Khamenei has not been publicly seen since he became supreme leader, following his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei’s assassination in US-Israeli strikes at the start of the Middle East war in February.
It also said that Khamenei ordered the commanders to update Iran’s target list to include “all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist (Israeli) enemy”.

stories.title: Syria weighing whether to join Makkah pact: foreign minister
summary: Syria’s Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani on Saturday said Damascus was considering whether to join the Makkah defence pact that binds Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.
Pakistan is providing “whatever support is needed” to defend Saudi Arabia amid the Houthi attacks, the military’s spokesperson Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said earlier this month.
In August, two weeks after the Makkah pact was signed, the Syrian foreign minister visited Pakistan and called on Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir.

stories.title: AI-based attendance system leads to dismissal of 72 doctors in Balochistan
summary: QUETTA: The Balochistan Health Department on Saturday dismissed 72 doctors from government service for prolonged absence from duty.

According to an official notification issued by the Balochistan health secretary, the action was taken under Section 4(B)(viii) of the Balochistan Employees’ Efficiency and Disciplinary Act (BEEDA), 2011.
In a statement, Balochistan Health Minister Bakht Muhammad Kakar said the doctors had repeatedly been issued notices directing them to report for duty, but they had failed to respond.

stories.title: Pakistan’s Punjab records 4.2 times more crop-fire detections than Indian Punjab: report
summary: LAHORE: Crop-fire detections in Pakistan’s Punjab were 4.2 times higher than in Indian Punjab during the first 29 days of October, according to satellite data, as the province grapples with worsening smog.

According to an analysis published by environmental monitoring website HamariHawa, Nasa satellites detected 13,241 fire spots in Pakistan’s Punjab between Oct 1 and 29, compared with 3,158 in Indian Punjab — 4.2 times as many detections.

A comparison based solely on data from the Suomi NPP satellite, which provides a consistent basis for examining trends over different years, showed that 4,562 fire spots were detected in Pakistan’s Punjab, compared with 918 in Indian Punjab, between Oct 1 and 29.

stories.title: ‘Very little, if anything, done for KP’: PM Shehbaz rails against PTI’s governance in province
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday criticised PTI’s governance in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, questioning whether the funds available to the now dysfunctional provincial government had been used transparently for the welfare and betterment of the people of the province.

Turning to the PTI, the prime minister said the party had spent the past two and a half years engaged in long marches and protests. “In 2014, Chinese President Xi Jinping was scheduled to visit Pakistan.
The prime minister recalled that the government had formed a committee comprising members of the PPP and PML-N to hold talks with the PTI. “Both sides held negotiations for 48 hours.

stories.title: UK PM 'open' to slavery apology but not reparations
summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Saturday he was “open” to the UK issuing a formal apology for its role in the transatlantic slave trade, but ruled out financial reparations.
Britain’s central role in slavery and the treatment of people in its former colonies has loomed over the 77-year-old monarch’s Caribbean tour.
The UK has never formally apologised for slavery nor or agreed to pay reparations.

stories.title: Capt Safdar's remarks about women suffering from illness draw criticism, including from CM Maryam
summary: LAHORE: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz’s spouse, retired Capt Muhammad Safdar, has come under fire for disparaging remarks about women advocating for bodily autonomy.
Speaking at a Khatm-i-Nabuwwat rally in Chiniot earlier this week, Safdar took aim at the slogan “mera jism, meri marzi” (my body, my choice).
Apart from CM Maryam, users on social media also took issue with Safdar’s remarks. “My [mother] has been a cancer patient, and God knows how we managed to get through those difficult times.

stories.title: Shooting at California Halloween store kills one, wounds six
summary: A shooting at a Halloween store in northern California killed one person and wounded six on Friday, police said, adding investigators had not yet identified who was responsible.
Fairfield Police Chief Dan Marshall told reporters one person was killed and six others were hospitalised with gunshot wounds.
The shooting took place near Florida Agricultural & Mechanical University’s campus on Perry Street, the university said, while police counted six adults and six juveniles among the injured.

stories.title: Prime suspect in Gujranwala bride's murder killed in alleged exchange of fire, claims CCD
summary: LAHORE: The Crime Control Department (CCD) claimed on Saturday that the prime suspect in the murder of a bride on her wedding day in Gujranwala district was killed during an alleged exchange of fire.
According to a CCD spokesperson, the prime suspect, Sarfraz, had allegedly been hiding in Karachi with the other suspects before being arrested.
A day earlier, the CCD claimed that two alleged robbers were “killed during an encounter” in Punjab’s Kasur.

stories.title: Court grants bail to anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan, lawyer confirms
summary: KARACHI: A judicial magistrate granted bail to anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan, his lawyer, Advocate Ahmad Masood, confirmed to Dawn on Saturday.
On October 22, the same judicial magistrate rejected a bail plea filed by Hassan, prompting the defence to challenge the rejection in a sessions court.
On October 17, Hassan was produced before Judicial Magistrate Memon upon the completion of his initial four-day physical remand.

stories.title: Singapore FM’s visit focused on enhancing cooperation in trade, infrastructure and digital technologies: FO
summary: The two ministers also exchanged a memorandum of understanding on cooperation in disaster management between Pakistan’s National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) and Singapore’s Civil Defence Force (SCDF).

On Friday, Dr Balakrishnan met Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir at the General Headquarters, where the two discussed regional security and avenues for bilateral cooperation.
The two sides also exchanged views on regional and international developments and reaffirmed their commitment to continued engagement and cooperation at bilateral and multilateral fora.

stories.title: Muslim Americans take on key electoral contests in midterms amid foreign policy debates
summary: The war in Gaza has fuelled demands for an end to US military support for Israel, while the war with Iran has raised questions about American intervention, regional stability and overseas military spending.

Many Muslim and Arab American voters are demanding that Washington reconsider its military support for Israel, although opposition to continued assistance also extends to progressive activists, younger Democrats and some Jewish Americans.
These issues could resonate well beyond Muslim communities, particularly as voters weigh overseas military commitments against domestic economic pressures.

stories.title: Three held for injuring scooty-riding female in Kasur
summary: KASUR: The A-Division police arrested three suspects on Friday for injuring a female college student by pushing her scooty at Baldia Chowk near the Government Girls College.

KABADDI: Sports inculcate discipline and a spirit of teamwork among youth and help them attain a healthy lifestyle, said Punjab Assembly Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmed Khan after a kabaddi match held at Khudian Khas in connection with Khelta Punjab on Friday.

He said the provincial government had initiated sports programmes to provide youth with a platform to showcase their talent and develop a healthy lifestyle instead of spending most of their time on mobile screens.

stories.title: Three-year-old child tests positive for mpox in Sindh
summary: KARACHI: Another child tested positive for mpox in the city on Friday, raising the tally of the viral infectious disease this year so far in the province to 115.
With the latest case, the total number of mpox cases reported this year so far at SIDH&RC has risen to 31, while in the province to 115 with 12 deaths.
The team sealed the facility following reports that a child seemed to have contracted mpox there.

stories.title: UK PM Burnham says he is 'open' to formal apology for slavery, but rules out reparations
summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was open to calls for a formal apology for Britain's historical role in slavery, ​before attending next week's Commonwealth summit at which he is likely ‌to face demands for financial reparations.

Writing in the Guardian newspaper, Burnham said Britain was "offering a structured dialogue with those affected by the transatlantic slave trade", in which at ​least 12.5 million Africans were abducted and sold into slavery.

Ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda next week, King Charles, who is touring the Caribbean, said it was "only right that we should ​acknowledge the great suffering ​and injustices of ⁠the past".

stories.title: Gen Z protests reach Germany as over 160,000 expected at Halloween rallies
summary: More than 160,000 people across Germany are expected to join demonstrations on Saturday, organisers say, as a youth-led movement inspired by protests elsewhere in Europe takes to the streets to demand better education and lower living costs.
The protests follow a wave of Gen Z-led demonstrations across Europe this year.
In Serbia, student-led activism helped unseat the country’s long-time leader at the ballot box, while protests in France have descended into rioting and looting.

stories.title: PM criticises PTI's 13-year rule in K-P, urges PML-N leadership to prioritise public welfare projects
summary: While criticising PTI, the prime minister said political slogans and divisive politics had taken precedence over public service, while problems in Peshawar, Kohistan, Hazara and the southern districts remained unaddressed.
PM Shehbaz was wary that the federal government had repeatedly called for collective efforts against terrorism, but its appeals had not received the desired response from the PTI-led government.
The premier said a decision had become necessary to protect the people, the country, the economy and society, adding that any delay could have caused further damage to the province.

stories.title: 1 killed, 6 injured in shooting at Halloween store in California
summary: Police responded to the shooting at a Spirit Halloween store in Solano Town Center in Fairfield around 8.30 pm Friday, according to ABC News.
On October 11, 9 people died in a shooting in Erie, Pennsylvania, where a 45-year-old man opened fire in a neighbourhood.

There have been more than 400 mass shootings in the US in 2026, according to data compiled by Gun Violence Archive, which defines a mass shooting ⁠as one ​in which four or more people are shot, excluding ​the shooter.

stories.title: Trump admin approves potential Patriot missiles sale to Ukraine
summary: The Trump administration on Friday green-lit the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine, the State Department said, but the Ukrainian president warned deliveries could take years.
The statement did not provide an estimate for when the weapons could be delivered to Ukraine.
The State Department said the weapons sale would be paid for with by donations from Ukraine’s allies but not with US funds.

stories.title: Trump administration plans to deport Afghan refugees to Pakistan: report
summary: The Trump administration is preparing to deport Afghan refugees to Pakistan as early as Monday, despite concerns that they could subsequently be returned to Afghanistan under Taliban rule, media reports said Friday.
AfghanEvac, an organisation advocating for Afghan refugees, criticised the administration’s reported deportation plans in a statement Friday.
The reported flight would come after months of uncertainty over the future of Afghan refugees at the Qatar facility, as the administration continues considering arrangements for their removal.

stories.title: Over 1,460 illegal medical centres sealed in 3 months in KP
summary: PESHAWAR: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Healthcare Commission has sealed 1,465 illegal medical centres across the province during the last three months, according to its latest performance report on Friday.
According to the commission’s spokesperson, Azam Rehman, measures were also taken to improve the registration and licensing of healthcare facilities and address public complaints.
The report stated that 610 new medical centres were registered during the last three months, bringing the total number of registered healthcare facilities in the province to 22,910.

stories.title: CM Maryam launches Rs2 trillion PIVOT initiative to boost industry, exports
summary: LAHORE: Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Friday officially launched the Punjab Innovation for Value, Opportunity and Transformation (PIVOT) Plan 2026-29 – around Rs2 trillion economic strategy aimed at positioning Punjab as an export-led industrial hub.
Speaking at the launch, the chief minister said: “Punjab is ready to move towards a new model of economic growth, driven by industry, innovation, value addition and exports.

Fatima Group Chairman Fawad Mukhtar expressed confidence that the business community would fully support the initiative, lauding the chief minister’s thorough engagement and declared that this venture represents the economic future of both Punjab and Pakistan.

stories.title: Anti-encroachment drive will continue regardless of political influence, says Talal
summary: The remarks came a day after the Capital Development Authority (CDA) issued an encroachment notice at Fazl's residence, identifying illegal constructions and encroachments on its land and directing their removal within 15 days.

The minister also cited operations carried out in the federal capital in this regard, saying that property was vacated behind the Prime Minister's House while illegal petrol pumps, marriage halls and other structures were removed along the Expressway.

Further, Chaudhry called on Fazl to answer the questions he had asked, arguing that in Peshawar, where houses of the poor or illegal buildings of businessmen on roads, in parks and on government land were being demolished, he claimed Fazl had occupied a road.

stories.title: Man sets himself ablaze outside court after daughter’s ‘rapist’ acquitted in Lahore
summary: LAHORE: A man set himself on fire outside the Muzaffargarh district courts on Friday, after an accused in the rape case of his daughter was acquitted after nine years of proceedings.
A court acquitted the rape case accused on Thursday for lack of evidence, nine years after the case was instituted.
The litigant said he had spent years pursuing the case and that his daughter had also been divorced by her husband because of rape.

stories.title: Man held in Karachi for swindling, blackmailing woman via matrimonial app
summary: KARACHI: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Friday claimed to have arrested a man for allegedly depriving a woman of approximately Rs4.45 million by making empty promises of marriage on a matrimonial app.
Man found shot dead A young man with an alleged criminal record was found shot dead in North Karachi on Friday, police and rescue services officials said.

Man killed as coach overturns A man was killed while five others were injured when a passenger coach overturned while avoiding a collision with a police mobile near Naval Colony gate in Baldia Town on Friday, police and rescue services officials said.

stories.title: Commuters risk life and limb as poles not removed from middle of road in Hyderabad
summary: HYDERABAD: Carpeting of a new road and opening it for traffic, despite many electricity poles still standing in the middle of the dual carriageway, has triggered a heated debate on social media as travelers risk life and limb.

Until now used to be known as Ghora Ground, the artery has been converted to an asphalt road, the landscape otherwise being an abandoned waterlogged area used for electricity transmission to Deh Fouj Gah through the poles.

He said proximity of Qasimabad grid station with the road necessitated relocation of electricity infrastructure, adding that until Wednesday (Oct 28), 97 poles had been shifted and the remaining ones would be relocated by Nov 10.

stories.title: SHC moved against construction on Karachi's Nehr-i-Khayyam
summary: KARACHI: The Jamaat-i-Islami, along with some Clifton residents, moved the Sindh High Court against the provincial government for carrying out construction and development activities on Nehr-i-Khayyam.

They asked the SHC to declare as illegal the alleged conversion, alteration or utilisation of the storm-water drain into a recreational park or commercial venture or any other inconsistent purpose without lawful authority and compliance with the applicable laws.
They urged the court to preserve Nehr-i-Khayyam for its lawful purpose and primary function as a storm-water drainage channel.

stories.title: Marka-e-Haq victory enhanced Pakistan's prestige: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif
summary: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said on Saturday that Pakistan's victory in Marka-e-Haq enhanced the country's international standing, Radio Pakistan reported.

The term Marka-e-Haq refers to the 2025 conflict with India, which began after India falsely blamed Pakistan for the April 22 Pahalgam attack and concluded with a ceasefire on May 10 following a successful Operation Bunyanun Marsoos launched by the country’s armed forces.

The 2025 Indo-Pak war The tensions between the nuclear-armed neighbours, Pakistan and India, escalated following the April 22 attack in Pahalgam, located in the Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (IIOJK), which claimed 26 lives.

stories.title: Mass protests sweep Italy during nationwide strike
summary: Tens of thousands of people, mostly students and workers, ​took to the streets across Italy on Friday to demand ‌higher wages and stronger public services, protest against the rising cost of living and oppose increased military spending.

Read: Four killed, 11 injured in Italian military helicopter crash in Bosnia, Herzegovina A large march passed near the Colosseum, in Rome, where protesters said they planned to set up ​tents and remain over the weekend.
In the evening, a large group tried to ‌march ⁠towards parliament, prompting police to use water cannon to disperse the crowd, Italian news agency ANSA reported.

stories.title: 2 Palestinians killed in Israel's ongoing violations of Gaza ceasefire
summary: A Palestinian was killed in an Israeli strike in central Gaza early Saturday, while another died of wounds sustained in an earlier attack, medical sources told Anadolu.
Israeli shelling reported across Gaza Meanwhile, local sources told Anadolu that Israeli military vehicles and artillery shelled several areas across the Gaza Strip.

Ceasefire violations leave over 1,500 dead Israeli violations of the Gaza ceasefire have killed 1,574 Palestinians and wounded 5,687 others as of Thursday, according to figures released by Gaza's Health Ministry.

stories.title: Karachi court approves Iqrarul Hassan's bail plea
summary: On October 13, Hassan was handed over to the NCCIA on a four-day physical remand.

On October 15, the District and Sessions Court East dismissed a petition challenging Hassan's physical remand, with the defence counsel questioning the legality of the proceedings and arguing that the case concerned digital and cyber matters.
Meanwhile, the NCCIA noted that no further investigation was required against Hassan; however, the forensic report was still awaited.

stories.title: Smoke-emitting vehicles fined in Lahore
summary: LAHORE: During the current month in Lahore, as many as 1,763 smoke-emitting vehicles were fined, while a total penalty of Rs5.5 million was imposed.
During the same period, 739 vehicles were impounded and overloaded vehicles were offloaded in Lahore.
Furthermore, 2,018 industrial units were inspected across the Lahore division, resulting in 41 units and 146 restaurants being sealed for causing pollution.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz forms body to review proposed LPG policy reforms
summary: The proposed reforms envisage allowing state-owned enterprises (SOEs) to enter the LPG import business and take over price-setting from the regulator, with prices subsequently passed on to the private sector.
Stakeholders said SOEs had limited LPG import experience and warned that the proposed levy on locally produced LPG would push prices higher, calling for a greater private-sector role.

A cabinet summary, seen by Dawn, proposes retaining monthly LPG pricing but removing Ogra’s role, with SOEs, including PSO, Sui companies, PARCO and Pakistan LNG, leading the shift to import-parity pricing.

stories.title: France braces for fresh unrest, government vows tough response
summary: France will deploy a 70,000-strong police presence to contain a widely expected bout of fresh unrest on Saturday in the latest nationwide protests driven by anger over living costs, public services and President Emmanuel Macron's government.

The nationwide demonstrations, which fall on Halloween, come two weeks after riots and looting caught security forces off guard, leaving damaged shops, public buildings and businesses in cities across France.
Read: ‘Threat exists’: Paris police warn of possible unrest ahead of protests Authorities are also alert to the possibility that rioters could use Halloween masks to conceal their identities.

stories.title: Barbs fly in Senate over rising poverty, PTI women’s detention
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Senate on Friday witnessed heated exchanges over rising poverty, the health and detention of PTI women leaders and activists, including Noreen Niazi, and an alleged increase in extrajudicial killings reaching Islamabad.
PTI Senator Azam Swati said he had spoken to Ms Niazi’s husband, who informed him that her treatment was progressing well. “He thanked the government for allowing her to meet her elder daughter.

The minister’s remarks that treatment would be determined by doctors rather than Ms Niazi’s wishes triggered protests and sloganeering by PTI members. “Let the House run, it will not work like this,” PPP Senator Shahadat Awan, who was presiding over the session, intervened.

stories.title: US approves $2.1 billion Patriot missile sale to Ukraine
summary: The US State Department said on Friday it approved the sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles to Ukraine for an estimated $2.1 billion, one of the most significant steps to supply defensive weapons to Kyiv since the start of the second Trump administration.
Ukraine has long said it urgently needs more missile interceptors to knock down ​the growing waves of missiles Russia's military fires at the country.
Lockheed previously announced Patriot PAC-3 missile interceptor production would go to 2,000 units ​annually.

stories.title: Qatari delegation arrives in Tehran for peace talks
summary: Iran retaliated with attacks on Israel and US assets, and has since blocked ships from using the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about a fifth of global oil consumption.
Separately, Iran said three oil tankers had been halted as they crossed the blockaded strait.
The gathering, held just days before the US midterm elections, also comes as global energy prices have soared since the US war on Iran began.

stories.title: Kamindu Mendis hits century as Sri Lanka go for a solid total
summary: Pakistan won the toss and opted to bowl first in the ODI tri-series final against Sri Lanka at the Gaddafi Stadium Lahore on Saturday.
We opted to field first as we had in mind that Sri Lanka batted second in the last four games," Pakistan's skipper Shaheen Afridi said.
Pakistan were outclassed by Sri Lanka in their previous game by eight wickets.

stories.title: KP police get tech to monitor counterterrorism operations
summary: PESHAWAR: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa police have integrated anti-drone systems and surveillance drones operating across the province into the Safe City Peshawar’s Command and Control Centre to strengthen security and surveillance capabilities.

Drones, anti-drone systems integrated into Peshawar’s Safe City network He said live monitoring of police operations, including those conducted by the CTD across the province, had also become possible, facilitating the timely sharing of information.

He said the integrated use of modern technology, drone surveillance, anti-drone systems and centralised monitoring would further strengthen the police’s operational capabilities, security surveillance and response to militant threats.
